title: fidelity/v2
description: targets/<id>/fidelity/<subject>-<n>.yaml (F11-R3; D-9 v3.12): one attestation that a subject — the root statement, or one definition in defs/ — says what its informal statement says, at one rung of the ladder. v2 adds `statement_hash`: D-9 grades a statement, not a subject name, so a certificate counts toward its subject's grade, signature count and signers only while its hash is the subject's current one, and a v1 certificate, which pins none, counts for nothing. Append-only: a certificate is never edited, and the latest counting certificate by (date, file name) is the subject's current grade. Above `mechanical-only` the attestor may not be the subject's author (D-9: the second rung is a non-author's signature), and the certificate names the exhibits the grade rests on. Versioned, never edited (D-34).

subject.description: `root`, or the name of a definition in the target's defs/.

statement_hash.description: SHA-256, lowercase hex, of the subject as it stood when the certificate was written: the root node's statement hash, or the definition file's content hash — the value the QA record pins for the same subject (F12-R5). A D-8 revision of the root or an edit of the definition changes it, and the certificate stops counting. A move of the graph's Mathlib pin does not.

grade.description: D-9 v3.12's ladder. Rung two is `screened-and-signed`; back-translation is one input to it, not the rung itself.

subject_author.description: Who wrote the subject. The first certificate for a subject establishes it; every later one must agree.

attestor.description: Who is signing. Equal to subject_author only at `mechanical-only`, which is the machine's own grade and signs for nobody.

evidence.description: What was checked, in the attestor's words. Free text, untrusted downstream (F11 §7).

evidence_files.description: Paths, relative to the graph root, of anything the evidence points at.

exhibits.description: The kernel-checked exhibits this grade rests on (D-9 v3.12). Empty at `mechanical-only`; F12 produces them for the mechanizable pass.
